learn.title: Iron-Air Batteries for Long Duration Storage
learn.intro: Iron-air batteries offer a breakthrough solution for storing renewable energy over weeks or months, addressing the critical need for long-duration energy storage. Unlike lithium-ion batteries that last hours, these systems can store power for 100+ hours, ensuring reliable clean energy even during extended cloudy or calm periods.
learn.c1_text: Iron-air batteries store energy by rusting iron rods inside the battery. During discharge, oxygen from the air reacts with iron to release electrons, generating electricity. Think of it like a controlled rusting process that's reversed when charging with renewable power. These batteries use abundant, cheap materials unlike scarce lithium or cobalt.
learn.c2_text: Iron-air batteries can store energy for 100+ hours compared to 4-6 hours for typical lithium-ion systems. They cost about 10 times less per kWh of storage capacity. The technology uses no rare earth elements, making it sustainable and geopolitically stable. Companies like Form Energy are pioneering commercial deployments.
learn.c3_text: India aims for 500 GW renewable capacity by 2030, requiring massive long-duration storage solutions. Iron-air batteries could complement India's pumped hydro projects. The government's National Energy Storage Programme supports such emerging technologies to ensure grid stability as solar and wind penetration increases significantly.
learn.stat1: Iron-air batteries can store energy for 100+ hours vs 4-6 hours for lithium-ion
learn.stat2: Cost advantage: 10x lower per kWh than lithium-ion batteries
learn.stat3: Global long-duration storage market projected to reach $50 billion by 2030

learn.title: Geothermal Energy: Harnessing Earth's Heat
learn.intro: Geothermal energy taps into the Earth's internal heat to generate clean electricity and provide heating solutions. This renewable resource offers consistent baseload power unlike intermittent solar and wind. With the potential to supply 25% of global electricity, geothermal represents a reliable pathway toward decarbonizing our energy systems sustainably.
learn.c1_text: Deep within Earth, radioactive decay generates immense heat reaching 6,000°C at the core. Geothermal plants tap into underground steam and hot water reservoirs just 1-3 km below surface. Like a natural nuclear plant, this heat flows continuously regardless of weather, providing 24/7 clean energy that complements variable renewables perfectly.
learn.c2_text: Three main approaches harness geothermal energy: dry steam plants use underground steam directly, flash steam plants convert high-pressure hot water to steam, and binary cycle plants use moderate-temperature water to heat a secondary fluid. The second method dominates globally, generating over 14 GW worldwide with remarkable efficiency rates above 90%.
learn.c3_text: India has identified 354 geothermal prospect locations across 12 states, with confirmed potential of 1,870 MW initially, potentially reaching 10,000 MW. The Himalayan region offers exceptional opportunities due to tectonic activity. Gujarat and Rajasthan lead exploration efforts, supported by the Ministry of Renewable Energy's focused geothermal program launched in 2008.
learn.stat3: India has identified 354 geothermal prospects across 12 states
learn.stat4: Geothermal plants operate at over 90% capacity factor

learn.title: Smart Grids and Advanced Metering Systems
learn.intro: Smart grids revolutionize electricity delivery through digital intelligence, enabling two-way communication between utilities and consumers. These systems optimize energy flow, prevent outages, and integrate distributed renewables seamlessly. As grids evolve to accommodate solar rooftops and electric vehicles, smart technologies become essential for maintaining reliability and efficiency.
learn.c1_text: Smart grids function like the internet for electricity, using sensors, meters, and communication networks to monitor and manage power flow in real-time. Advanced meters record consumption every 15 minutes instead of monthly readings. This enables utilities to detect outages instantly, balance supply-demand dynamically, and provide consumers with detailed usage insights for better energy management.
learn.c2_text: Smart grids excel at managing variable renewable sources by predicting generation patterns and adjusting distribution accordingly. When solar farms produce excess power midday, smart systems redirect surplus to storage or high-demand areas. Conversely, during low wind periods, they can activate backup resources seamlessly. This flexibility supports higher renewable penetration while maintaining grid stability and power quality standards.
learn.c3_text: India launched its National Smart Grid Mission in 2013, planning installation of 250 million smart meters by 2025. States like Karnataka and Tamil Nadu lead pilot projects integrating solar microgrids with smart technologies. The initiative supports India's target of 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030, requiring intelligent grid management to handle distributed renewable energy sources effectively.
learn.stat1: Smart grids reduce outage duration by 30-50%
learn.stat2: Advanced meters sample electricity use every 15 minutes
learn.stat3: India plans 250 million smart meter installations by 2025
learn.stat4: Smart grid investments reached $120 billion globally in 2023

learn.title: India's EV Policy and PM e-DRIVE Scheme
learn.intro: India's electric vehicle policy framework aims to transform transportation through the PM e-DRIVE scheme and state-level initiatives. Targeting 30% EV adoption by 2030, these policies address air pollution, oil import dependence, and climate goals. With over 1.4 million EVs already on roads, India is rapidly scaling its clean mobility ecosystem for sustainable urban transport.
learn.c1_text: Launched in 2017 with ₹10,000 crore budget, PM e-DRIVE provides subsidies for electric buses, cars, and two-wheelers. The Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid & Electric vehicles scheme incentivizes purchases while building charging infrastructure. Subsidies range from ₹1 lakh for cars to ₹10,000 for two-wheelers, accelerating consumer adoption and manufacturer investment in EV production across India.
learn.c2_text: States like Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, and Karnataka have introduced additional incentives beyond central schemes. Tamil Nadu offers 100% road tax exemption and registration fee waivers. Some states provide direct cash incentives up to ₹1.5 lakh for EV buyers. These complementary policies create competitive environments driving faster EV adoption and manufacturing localization across different regions.
learn.c3_text: India's Production Linked Incentive scheme allocates ₹18,000 crore for automotive manufacturing, attracting companies like Tesla, Tata Motors, and Mahindra. Over 30 EV models are now available domestically. The government aims to establish 300 GW renewable capacity by 2030 to power this growing EV fleet, creating integrated clean transportation and energy ecosystems.
learn.stat2: Over 1.4 million EVs currently on Indian roads
learn.stat4: PLI scheme allocates ₹18,000 crore for auto manufacturing

learn.title: Green Hydrogen Production Through Electrolysis
learn.intro: Green hydrogen produced via water electrolysis using renewable electricity represents a crucial clean fuel for hard-to-abate sectors like steel, shipping, and aviation. As the world's largest hydrogen producer, India's National Green Hydrogen Mission allocates $2.3 billion to become a global manufacturing hub. This technology bridges renewable energy generation with industrial decarbonization effectively.
learn.c1_text: Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolyzers operate at higher current densities, respond quickly to variable renewable input, and require less space but use expensive platinum catalysts. Alkaline systems are cheaper, use abundant nickel catalysts, and handle large-scale production efficiently but respond slower to power fluctuations. Both split water into hydrogen and oxygen using clean electricity.
learn.c2_text: Green hydrogen can replace fossil-derived hydrogen in ammonia production, steelmaking, and refinery operations. When burned, it emits only water vapor, making it ideal for high-temperature industrial processes where batteries fall short. The technology enables seasonal energy storage, converting excess renewable power into transportable hydrogen fuel for later use during peak demand periods.
learn.c3_text: India's $2.3 billion National Green Hydrogen Mission aims to make the country a global manufacturing hub, targeting 5 MMT annual production by 2030. Reliance Industries plans $70 billion investment in green hydrogen projects. The initiative includes 100 manufacturing units and 20 strategic projects, positioning India as a key exporter to meet global clean energy transition demands.

learn.stat2: Target: 5 million metric tons annual green hydrogen production by 2030

learn.stat4: Green hydrogen can replace 15% of global fossil fuel consumption

learn.title: Direct Air Carbon Capture Technology
learn.intro: Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology removes carbon dioxide directly from ambient air using chemical processes powered by clean energy. While not a substitute for emission reductions, DAC provides a vital tool for achieving net-zero goals by addressing historical emissions. With costs declining from $600 to $100-300 per ton, this technology offers scalable atmospheric cleanup solutions for climate restoration.
learn.c1_text: DAC systems use large fans to pull ambient air through chemical filters containing amines or potassium hydroxide that bind with CO2 molecules. Once saturated, the filters undergo heating or pressure changes to release pure CO2 for storage or utilization. Unlike point-source capture from smokestacks, DAC works anywhere, removing legacy emissions scattered throughout the atmosphere systematically.
learn.c2_text: DAC requires substantial energy input—approximately 300-500 kWh per ton of CO2 captured. Solar and wind power make the process truly carbon-negative when accounting for capture energy needs. Some facilities integrate directly with renewable installations, using excess power during peak generation periods. This symbiotic relationship maximizes both clean energy utilization and carbon removal capacity simultaneously.
learn.c3_text: Current global DAC capacity exceeds 10 million tons annually across 30+ facilities. Costs range from $100-600 per ton depending on technology and energy sources. Iceland's Orca plant captures 4,000 tons annually using geothermal power. The US Department of Energy offers $3.5 billion in funding for DAC projects. India is exploring DAC integration with its expanding renewable energy infrastructure.
